label: Damascus goat

names.text: Names taken from the infobox and the introduction of the Damascus goat page: Aleppo, Baladi, Chami, Halep and Shami. The page says Halep refers to Aleppo, Shami and Chami to Greater Syria, and Baladi means local.

about.text: Damascus is a dual-purpose goat breed from Greater Syria, named after Damascus, and reared for both milk and meat. In Syria its average yield is about 375 kg per lactation with 4.76 percent butterfat, and southern Turkey reports 500 to 600 kg.

sources.text: Taken from the Damascus goat page: the Greater Syria origin, the dual-purpose use, the Syrian yield and butterfat figures, and the southern Turkey yield range.
The infobox and introduction give Greater Syria as the country of origin and say the breed is named after Damascus. The page gives no founding date, so none is recorded.

The Use section says average yield in Syria is approximately 375 kg per lactation. The same section gives 500 to 600 kg for southern Turkey, which is not in this record because it is another country's figure. The year was not stated.
The Use section gives butter-fat content of 4.76 percent in Syria. No protein or lactose figure was given.
The Use section describes it as a dual-purpose breed, reared both for milk and for meat.
The infobox says FAO (2007) lists it as not at risk. The page text also says DAD-IS (2026) lists it as not at risk, which was not checked on DAD-IS directly.

facts.v: A goat of this breed ranked first at the Mazayen al-Maaz goat beauty contest in Riyadh in 2008.

sources.text: Taken from the Use section of the Damascus goat page.

gaps: No founding date, no current population (the page says Syria has reported no data since 2006, when the estimate was 61,447 head), no lactation length and no protein figure were found. The yield range was combined from the Syrian and southern Turkish figures and does not come from one record.
